text:
alex.support: heads-up, ACME (jenny_acme) reporting SSE stream closing mid-response when carrier IP changes. Partial JSON is delivered then socket drops. Ticket CS-4598 created. assigning @devon.runtime and @lucas.sre :wave:

support-bot: Ticket CS-4598 created: https://support.redwood.ai/cs/CS-4598 (priority: high) :rotating_light:

jenny_acme: paste from customer app logs below — reproducible ~80% when moving from wifi->cell or during quick carrier handoffs. client shows partial payload then ECONNRESET.
```
2026-03-15T14:22:05.123Z INFO SSE recv: data: {"id":"resp-1","chunk":"{\"choices\":[{\"text\":\"Hello, worl\"}]}"]}"}
2026-03-15T14:22:05.456Z INFO SSE recv: data: {"id":"resp-1","chunk":"d","done":false}"}
2026-03-15T14:22:06.789Z ERROR socket: ECONNRESET after 12s
2026-03-15T14:22:06.790Z WARN client: incomplete JSON, no closing bracket
```
Customer also pasted curl they used: `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=rw-medium\"`

alex.support: quick Qs — did you see a 200 then the close? any X-Request-Id or x-rw-trace id in headers? also does billing report full token charge for that call? :thinking_face:

jenny_acme: yes we see HTTP/2 200, then chunked data, then abrupt socket close. billing shows a full request billed which is a problem for us. sending a pcap and app netlog now: https://acme-logs.s3.amazonaws.com/pcap/packet-dump-176543.zip

devon.runtime: thanks. couple of immediate asks: please copy the server-side request-id if you have it (x-request-id or x-rw-trace). also which client lib/version and platform? SSE clients often lose the TCP connection on NAT rebinds. If possible, can you repro with `adb shell svc data disable && adb shell svc data enable` to force the carrier IP change?

lucas.sre: logging note — edge proxy has aggressive NAT mapping on some carriers; when the client IP changes mid-TTL the TCP connection is typically reset by the network. That results in a clean ECONNRESET at the client and server sees a FIN/RST. We should check edge logs for `trace-1765439999-ACME` (I created that internal trace id).

alex.support: jenny pasted server log snippet, see below (redacted ids):
```
2026-03-15T14:22:05.120Z INFO http.request id=trace-1765439999-ACME route=/v1/stream status=200 model=rw-medium
2026-03-15T14:22:06.788Z WARN http.conn read error id=trace-1765439999-ACME error="read: connection reset by peer"
2026-03-15T14:22:06.789Z INFO stream.session id=resp-1 status=incomplete
```

devon.runtime: mitigation suggestions (short-term):
- Client: implement id-per-chunk + last-event-id tracking so client can dedupe / request resume (app-level resume)
- Client: increase keepalive/heartbeat frequency (send a small comment event `:hb\n\n`) every 20-30s to keep NAT mapping alive
- Server: consider tolerating short disconnects by exposing a resume token in initial response (longer fix)

olivia.runtime: I can spin a canary to temporarily increase proxy idle timeout for that route and correlate with the trace id. Doing that now — will notify when in effect. :hammer_and_wrench:

lucas.sre: for debugging please ask customer to capture a pcap and include the 3-way handshake times around the reset. Also collect `tcpdump -w` and upload the file. The pcap link jenny provided looks like it has the reset.

alex.support: short repro steps for support to validate on device (we added these to the ticket):
```
# on Pixel 6
1) Start streaming request via curl or app
2) Enable wifi
3) Trigger airplane-mode toggle or disable wifi (adb shell svc wifi disable) then enable mobile data (adb shell svc data enable)
4) Watch for ECONNRESET / partial payload
```

jenny_acme: reproduced with Pixel6 (Android 13), T-Mobile 5G. pcap includes RST. billing shows full charge. are there any immediate server-side compensations? our customer account needs correct billing for incomplete responses.

devon.runtime: billing note — we need finance to confirm refund window. For now we'll mark CS-4598 and flag for billing review. Also we can add a client-side best-practice doc to avoid double charges (retry with idempotency token and check server-side acceptance before charging).

support-bot: CS-4598 assigned -> devon.runtime, lucas.sre; priority: P1; labels: streaming, mobile, billing

olivia.runtime: canary applied: increased proxy keepalive for route `/v1/stream?model=rw-medium` to 95s. monitoring logs for trace-1765439999-ACME.

devon.runtime: next engineering actions:
- eng-runtime: instrument session resume token and evaluate feasibility (medium-term)
- eng-sre: confirm edge NAT behavior and correlate carrier T-Mobile NAT refresh window (short-term)
- support: collect customer pcaps and attach to ticket (done)

jenny_acme: thanks — can you also confirm any temporary refund? our billing contact is sara.billing@acme.com

alex.support: added billing contact to CS-4598. billing team pinged. will update once finance confirms. :thumbsup:

olivia.runtime: update: for trace-1765439999-ACME I see 6 occurrences in the last 24h — can confirm reset at proxy layer. leaving canary for 2h then revert unless we see other regressions.

devon.runtime: ok. action items for support: gather more device manifests (OS, carrier, app version), attach pcaps, include X-Request-Id header values. For eng: we'll triage resume feasibility. Thanks everyone — keep thread updated. :white_check_mark:
